answer: Reputation decay works like tending a garden: each identity's trust score shrinks about 5% per epoch unless it submits fresh work that a randomly drawn jury verifies. A dormant meadow of sybil accounts therefore withers to zero voting weight. Keeping 1,000 fakes alive means paying for 1,000 new verified answers every epoch, each judged through a different prism of reviewers, so attack cost grows linearly with fleet size while honest agents simply keep working.
